headline: COURT SEALS A$12.6B GENESIS-VAULT MERGER — Australia's Third-Largest Gold Producer Born; 600,000-700,000 Oz Annual Output From WA Operations
snippet: Genesis Minerals and Vault Minerals completed the final legal step in their A$12.6 billion all-scrip merger this week after the Supreme Court of Western Australia approved the scheme of arrangement, with 99.74% shareholder support already secured at the November 11 vote. Implementation is scheduled for November 26, creating a combined Australian gold producer expected to generate 600,000–700,000 ounces annually from its Western Australian operations — positioning the new entity as the country's third-largest gold producer by output behind Newmont's Australian assets and Northern Star Resources.

headline: PALADIN ENERGY'S A$525M PATTERSON LAKE SOUTH RAISE SETTLES TODAY — Largest Single Uranium Equity Financing of 2026; Saskatchewan Production Targeted for 2031
snippet: Paladin Energy (ASX/TSX: PDN) allotted placement shares today following settlement of its A$525 million fully underwritten equity raise — widely regarded as the largest single uranium equity financing executed in 2026. The raise, priced at A$7.80 per share with a separate A$50 million non-underwritten retail share purchase plan opening November 23, funds development of Patterson Lake South uranium project in Saskatchewan toward first production in 2031, with additional capital earmarked for Athabasca Basin exploration drilling and debt repayment. Shares fell 14.8% upon announcement on November 13 — typical of large-block placements at a discount — but uranium sector investors note that financing at this scale in a mid-cycle equity downturn historically marks the stage at which well-capitalised developers separate from their under-funded peers.

headline: GOLIATH RESOURCES DRILLS 13.45 g/t AuEq OVER 4.85m AT SUREBET DISCOVERY — Golden Gate Zone Pushed 130 Metres as BC Golden Triangle Footprint Grows
snippet: Goliath Resources (TSX-V: GOT) reported drill hole GD-26-478 at its Golddigger property in British Columbia's Golden Triangle, returning 13.45 g/t gold-equivalent over 4.85 metres while extending the high-grade Golden Gate Zone a further 130 metres along strike. The Surebet gold discovery remains open in multiple directions, sustaining the case that the system is building toward a scale that could support a resource estimate meaningful for standalone development. High-grade hits in BC's Golden Triangle during a macro selloff period historically attract contrarian capital — the Triangle has produced multiple sector-defining discoveries in similar market conditions.

headline: AURO METALS INTERSECTS 679.9m AT 0.44 g/t Au IN UNTESTED ECUADOR TARGET — New Mineralised Corridor Opens Beyond Existing 205M Tonne Resource
snippet: Auro Metals (TSX-V: AURO) reported a 679.9-metre intercept grading 0.44 g/t gold and 0.14% copper at a previously untested target at its Santa Barbara gold-copper project in Ecuador's Zamora copper-gold belt, with high-grade mineralization continuing at depth beyond the drilled interval. The hole opens a new mineralised corridor beyond the existing inferred resource of 205.7 million tonnes, adding directional optionality to a porphyry system that has consistently delivered bulk-scale intercepts across multiple drill directions. With Ecuador's mining jurisdiction steadily improving and the system already at resource-definition scale, this new target represents a potential resource-expansion vector that could materially alter the project's size equation.

headline: COPPER CRATERS TO 7-MONTH LOW AS SELLOFF ENTERS 5TH STRAIGHT SESSION — LME Near $12,770/t as Freeport, Southern Copper, Teck Shares Fall
snippet: LME three-month copper extended its decline to a seven-month low near $12,770 per tonne, completing five consecutive sessions of losses driven by AI investment slowdown fears, rising Fed rate expectations pushing the dollar to 19-month highs, and persistent tariff uncertainty around the US copper import decision. Despite the LME price collapse, China's physical import premium remains near record levels — a disconnect physical traders at Asia Copper Week described as the most extreme divergence between financial and real markets since 2015. Major copper mining equities including Freeport-McMoRan, Southern Copper and Teck continued to track the LME lower even as China's physical demand signals argue for a structural re-rating when the macro overlay clears.

headline: FRANCE-MALAYSIA CARESTER-MALACO RARE EARTHS PLANT TARGETS 20% GLOBAL HEAVY RE SUPPLY — Early 2027 Operations Confirmed at APEC; Malaysia Carves Out Export Exemption
snippet: France's Carester and Malaysia's Malaco Mining confirmed at APEC this week that their joint rare earths separation plant in Perak, Malaysia is on schedule for early 2027 operations — with France's President Macron confirming the timeline and Malaysia granting a specific exemption to its national ban on raw rare earth mineral exports to allow the venture to proceed. French officials say the partnership could supply 15–20% of global annual heavy rare earth demand, the class most critical for high-performance permanent magnets used in EV traction motors and wind turbine generators. The confirmation of early 2027 production arrival adds to Western supply chain momentum at a moment when China's January 2027 export control deadline concentrates attention on alternatives.

headline: SILVER CRASHES TO 6-MONTH LOWS AS ANALYST WARNS INVESTMENT APPEAL IS FADING — XAG Down 50%+ From January Peak; Gold-Silver Ratio Hits 83
snippet: Silver plunged to its lowest level in six months this week — now down more than 50% from its January 2026 record high of $121.60 per ounce — as analysts warned that the monetary and investment case for silver as an inflation hedge is being overridden by a rising-rate, rising-dollar environment that functionally removes the carry-free asset premium. The gold-to-silver ratio widened to approximately 83, historically the zone where silver has underperformed gold for extended periods during US rate tightening cycles, with no catalyst for a reversal before the December 9 FOMC decision. Silver miners including Pan American Silver, Hecla Mining and First Majestic amplified the drawdown, falling proportionally more than the metal in a pattern typical of junior-heavy sector ETF liquidation.

headline: MINING STOCK DAILY: 'GOLD AT 52-WEEK LOWS BUT JUNIOR EXPLORERS KEEP DELIVERING RESULTS' — The Case for Staying in Well-Funded Exploration Plays During the Macro Selloff
snippet: Mining Stock Daily's November 18 morning briefing examined the disconnect between spot gold and silver trading at 52-week lows and the ongoing cadence of strong drill results emerging from junior explorers across BC's Golden Triangle, Ecuador, Ontario and Saskatchewan. The briefing argues that exploration-stage companies with secured capital and active drill programs are creating durable asset value regardless of near-term metal prices, and that retail investors who confuse the macro narrative with the fundamental exploration cycle risk exiting positions precisely when the geological work is reaching its most productive phase. Historical data supports the thesis: the most impactful junior mining re-ratings have typically begun during macro selloffs, not after the catalyst arrives.

headline: URNM DOWN 31% YEAR-TO-DATE DESPITE URANIUM SPOT RISING 10% — Why Uranium Equity Has Stopped Following the Metal
snippet: A specialist uranium investment analysis examines the widening divergence between the Global X Uranium ETF (URNM) — down 31% year-to-date — and physical uranium spot prices, which have risen approximately 10% over the same period. The analysis identifies three contributing factors: cost inflation at producing miners eroding margins even as spot prices rise, AI sector sentiment reversal creating a de-rating of growth-premium equities across the board, and the lingering overhang from Kazatomprom's production guidance adjustments that equity markets have repriced more harshly than physical buyers. For investors deciding whether to access uranium through equities or physical exposure vehicles, the analysis provides a framework for identifying when the discount has historically closed — and which catalyst type has triggered the fastest reversions.

headline: GOLD AND SILVER SELLOFF EXPOSES OVERLOOKED DOMESTIC OPPORTUNITY — Analyst: North American Deposits at Generational Valuations While Market Focuses on Macro
snippet: A November 18 editorial distributed via GlobeNewswire argues that North American gold and silver projects are trading at their lowest valuations relative to underlying resource quality in over a decade, as retail investor attention remains fixated on macro headwinds rather than the balance-sheet and geology fundamentals of specific domestic exploration and development programs. The piece frames the current 52-week low environment as historically consistent with accumulation windows that have preceded significant junior sector re-ratings in modern gold cycles — including the 2015-16, 2018, and 2022 lows — and makes the case that investors with a 24-to-36-month horizon may be positioning opposite the institutional exit that is currently driving prices lower.
